current_answer: An expiring Microsoft for Startups balance is not an automatic path to more Azure credits. Microsoft says its credits cannot be extended or transferred, and use outside covered services or in another billing profile can still generate charges. The investor offer needs an affiliated organisation’s referral code. A separate new-to-Azure startup offer lists USD 1,000 for 90 days and another USD 4,000 for 180 days after business verification; it is not a top-up for existing recipients. Microsoft’s no-code application pages still conflict on a USD 200 versus USD 1,000 starter balance, so check the live account before planning spend.

catalogue_card.question: Can you renew expiring Microsoft startup credits without an investor code?
catalogue_card.text: If your Microsoft startup credits are nearly gone, a new-to-Azure offer is not a top-up. Microsoft says existing credits cannot be extended or transferred; investor benefits require a referral code. Two issuer guides still disagree on the no-code starter amount, so check your account balance and billing profile before planning spend.

summary: Microsoft says its startup credits cannot be extended or transferred, and uncovered use or a different billing profile may generate charges.
A new-to-Azure startup can seek USD 1,000 for 90 days and another USD 4,000 for 180 days after business verification; this is not an existing-recipient top-up.
The Investor Network offer needs a referral code. The no-code guides still conflict on USD 200 versus USD 1,000 starting credit.
Interledger Local Impact remains paused; NLnet still lists 3 November 2026, 12:00 CET.
uncertainty: Microsoft has not published a general top-up route for an existing recipient without an investor referral in the reviewed documents.
Two current Microsoft no-code guides still conflict on the starter amount.
The India founder account is self-reported and does not establish typical approval, credit policy, or support outcomes.
